queue_items.class: E-05 count-object / scoped digit (with E-06 register)
queue_items.claim: The row's part-scoped vocative digit misreports the very inventory it cites: the range holds five bni_address verses, not four.
queue_items.grounds: prov_device_inventory.json bni_address declares count_object 'verses containing the word-bound VOCATIVE token beni (my son; chirik), any position, pointed tier (E-1 corrected)', count 22, by_chapter 3:3 and 4:2; its refs inside Prov.3.1-Prov.4.27 are Prov.3.1, Prov.3.11, Prov.3.21, Prov.4.10 and Prov.4.20 - FIVE. My independent sweep agrees: over consonantal_index.json, the word-bound skeleton בני returns 30 verses / 30 tokens book-wide, of which 22 carry the chirik vocative (both attested spellings, with and without dagesh in the bet: 19 + 3) and 8 the tsere construct, i.e. exactly the inventory's 22, one token per verse - so the row's '22 tokens book-wide' happens to coincide numerically while naming the wrong unit (the inventory counts verses). The omitted verse is Prov.3.11, where the vocative stands as word 3, מוּסַ֣ר יְ֭הוָה בְּנִ֣י (oshb:Prov.3.11, words 1-3, byte tier); it drops out only under a verse-initial-opening count object, which the row never names while citing an any-position inventory. Not load-bearing for the seam: word 1 of oshb:Prov.3.1 is בְּ֭נִי at byte tier and the row closes on the PE at Prov.3.4 (pmarks, PE, tier-3 weak, single-witness), both independently verified, and the divine-name contrast the row draws is byte-true (no word-bound YHWH token anywhere in Prov.3.1-Prov.3.4; five across Prov.3.5-Prov.3.12).
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair, text register, count object named and digit re-derived - e.g. 'the vocative opens Prov.3.1 and recurs verse-initially at Prov.3.21, Prov.4.10 and Prov.4.20 (word-bound vocative verses across Prov.3-4: 5, the fifth at Prov.3.11 standing mid-verse; 22 verses book-wide)'; drop 'the part' and the inventory name from row prose.

trigger_dispositions.grounds: Both arms fail. TEST 1: 'within the part' and 'four heading this part' describe the writer's work unit rather than the text, and the same sentence names a staging inventory in row prose ('bni_address inventory') - the register rule bars tooling names and requires cross-row reference to be verse-anchored. TEST 2: the reference carries a scoped count claim, and re-derived from the inventory it names the digit is wrong - five bni_address verses stand inside Prov.3.1-Prov.4.27, not four. Recorded as the medium finding below.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: בְּ֭נִי (oshb:Prov.3.1) opens both the row and the part, the first of four bni_address occurrences within the part, recurring at 3.21, 4.10, and 4.20 (bni_address inventory: 22 tokens book-wide, four heading this part). Two imperative-plus-consequence couplets follow: retain the father's teaching for length of days (3.1-3.2), then bind kindness and truth on the heart for favor with God and man (3.3-3.4). The row closes at the petuchah after Prov.3.4 (oshb:Prov.3.4, single-witness), where אֱלֹהִ֣ים (oshb:Prov.3.4) is the divine name named once; the couplets beginning at 3.5 each name the divine name יְ֭הוָה (oshb:Prov.3.5) directly, while neither couplet in 3.1-3.4 does.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the row through 3.12 was rejected because the couplets from 3.5 onward each name the divine name יְ֭הוָה (oshb:Prov.3.5) directly, a naming shift the petuchah at 3.4 (oshb:Prov.3.4, single-witness) corroborates but does not itself drive.

shipped_row.device_notes: Synonymous parallelism binds each couplet's two half-lines -- teaching and commandments at web:Prov.3.1 “My son, don’t forget my teaching, but let your heart keep my commandments,” and kindness and truth at 3.3; the neck-and-heart-tablet figure of 3.3 gives the abstract virtue pair a concrete, wearable image.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The chapter opens immediately after the petuchah that closes Wisdom's opening speech (oshb:Prov.1.33 (petuchah, single-witness)), with the chapter's one vocative, occurring once across its 22 verses, בְּ֭נִי אִם תִּקַּ֣ח 'my son, if you receive' (oshb:Prov.2.1), launching three protases (2.1, 2.3, 2.4: receive my words, cry out for understanding, seek her like silver) plus one purpose-infinitive clause (2.2: incline your ear to wisdom) running through Prov.2.4. The initial apodosis follows immediately, אָ֗ז תָּ֭בִין 'then you will understand' (oshb:Prov.2.5), naming the fear of Yahweh as the reward. Its opening word collates byte-identical against the word opening the second apodosis at oshb:Prov.2.9 (byte tier), which announces the same reward in terms of righteousness, justice, and equity. A purpose-clause pair follows on the same pattern: לְ֭הַצִּ֣ילְךָ 'to deliver you' opens Prov.2.12 (oshb:Prov.2.12), naming deliverance first from evil men (Prov.2.12-Prov.2.15) and then, in a byte-identical repetition of the same infinitive at oshb:Prov.2.16 (byte tier), from the strange woman (Prov.2.16-Prov.2.19). A concluding exhortation, לְמַ֗עַן 'therefore' (oshb:Prov.2.20), draws the chapter to its antithetic close, “But the wicked will be cut off from the land. The treacherous will be rooted out of it.” (web:Prov.2.22), the verse carrying the chapter's own petuchah (oshb:Prov.2.22 (petuchah, single-witness)).
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A finer strophic split at the recurring 'then'/'to deliver you' markers (Prov.2.1-Prov.2.4, Prov.2.5-Prov.2.11, Prov.2.12-Prov.2.19, Prov.2.20-Prov.2.22) was considered and is textually real, but the chapter's vocative fires exactly once across its 22 verses and the chapter is grammatically one long sentence from protasis to conclusion, so it is kept as one row at some cost to the four-to-eight-verse span typical for instruction_lecture units elsewhere in this collection.

prev_row.device_notes: Ketiv/qere notes attach to two verses inside this span: oshb:Prov.2.7 and oshb:Prov.2.8 (both ketiv/qere, single-witness), sitting inside the first apodosis section. The protasis clauses of Prov.2.1-Prov.2.4 and the apodosis clauses of Prov.2.5-Prov.2.11 run on synonymous parallelism, restating one recurring appeal and one recurring reward in parallel cola, with the closing couplet turning antithetic (Prov.2.21-Prov.2.22: the upright remain in the land, but the wicked are cut off).

next_row.boundary_rationale: From 3.5 through 3.12 four imperative-plus-consequence couplets each name the divine name -- trust (3.5-3.6), fear and turn from evil (3.7-3.8), honor with substance (3.9-3.10), and accept discipline (3.11-3.12): the divine name is named once each in 3.5, 3.7, 3.9, 3.11, 3.12 (5 tokens across the row's 8 verses), absent from 3.6, 3.8, 3.10, a naming density that sets these couplets apart from the teaching-retention pair of 3.1-3.4, where the divine name is named only once, as אֱלֹהִ֣ים (oshb:Prov.3.4). The petuchah after Prov.3.10 (oshb:Prov.3.10, single-witness) falls inside the row, between the honor couplet and the discipline couplet, without ending it: both keep the same imperative-plus-consequence shape and both name the divine name, so the mark corroborates an internal pause rather than the row's own edge. The row ends before 3.13, where the address shifts from second-person imperative to a third-person beatitude formula.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the row at the petuchah after 3.10 (oshb:Prov.3.10, single-witness) was considered and set aside: the honor couplet before it and the discipline couplet after it keep the same construction and both name the divine name (יְ֭הוָה, oshb:Prov.3.9; יְ֭הוָה, oshb:Prov.3.11), so the mark falls inside one naming-density unit rather than at its edge.
observed_substrate_signals: the divine name is named once each in 3.5, 3.7, 3.9, 3.11, 3.12 (5 tokens across the row's 8 verses; word-bound accent_stripped sweep restricted to the row's own span), absent from 3.6, 3.8, 3.10

next_row.device_notes: Each couplet pairs synonymous halves (trust/lean at 3.5, fear/turn at 3.7); the fourth couplet (3.11-3.12) varies the pattern with a father-son simile rather than a bodily-benefit result, a texture shift within the shared construction.

queue_items.claim: The rival narrower cut is rejected first on the ABSENCE of a parashah/disclosure object, an inference the book's mark law forbids.
queue_items.grounds: The strongest_rejected_alternative reads that a cut after 3.24 'lacks any parashah or disclosure-object support, and both halves keep the same second-person, self-directed object, so the wider bound is kept instead'. The absence is byte-true - pmarks_Prov.json carries PE at Prov.3.18 and PE at Prov.3.35 with nothing between, and neither paseq nor K/Q anywhere in Prov.3.21-Prov.3.26 - but pmarks_Prov.json marks_note states in terms 'Absence is NEVER counterevidence', and the book strategy repeats it for the Writings parashah layer, so the first of the two grounds offered against the rival is inadmissible. It is not alone load-bearing: the second ground (both halves keep the same second-person, self-directed object) is positive and textual and stands on its own, and the row's own edges are untouched - the vocative בְּ֭נִי at oshb:Prov.3.21 (word 1, byte tier) and the object shift at Prov.3.27. Note the contrast within the same row: the in-span statement 'No petuchah or other disclosure-object note falls inside this span' is proper disclosure and is byte-true; only its conversion into a reason against the rival is the defect.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair: rest the rival's rejection on the positive ground alone (the shared second-person, self-directed object across 3.21-3.24 and 3.25-3.26) and delete the 'lacks any parashah or disclosure-object support' clause; keep the in-span absence statement where it stands, as disclosure.

trigger_dispositions.grounds: TEST 1 fails: 'the part's second lecture-opening slot' names the writer's work unit and orders the claim by row sequence, where the register rule requires a verse-anchored text fact. TEST 2: the enumerated verses are byte-true - Prov.3.1, Prov.4.10 and Prov.4.20 are each bni_address verses (prov_device_inventory.json) and word 1 of oshb:Prov.3.21 is בְּ֭נִי at byte tier - but the ordinal 'second' is derived from the row set rather than from bytes: against the inventory's own count object Prov.3.21 is the third of the five vocative verses in Prov.3.1-Prov.4.27. A true claim carried in workflow register, so low, recorded below.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: בְּ֭נִי (oshb:Prov.3.21) reopens second-person address at 3.21, the part's second lecture-opening slot (matching 3.1, 4.10, 4.20). The row keeps sound wisdom and discretion before the addressee's eyes as one extended promise: life and grace (3.21-3.22), secure walking and untroubled sleep (3.23-3.24), and freedom from sudden fear because יְ֭הוָה (oshb:Prov.3.26) is the addressee's confidence (3.25-3.26). No petuchah or other disclosure-object note falls inside this span; the row ends before 3.27, where the object of each admonition shifts from the addressee's own wisdom-keeping to the addressee's neighbor.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A narrower cut after 3.24, separating the wisdom-admonition (3.21-3.24) from the fear-admonition (3.25-3.26), lacks any parashah or disclosure-object support, and both halves keep the same second-person, self-directed object, so the wider bound is kept instead.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The row opens with אַשְׁרֵ֣י (oshb:Prov.3.13) governing 'the man' in third person, a genre break from the second-person imperative address running since 3.1 -- the tier-1 signal opening the poem the strategy flags as a bounds-argue candidate. The praise of wisdom continues through 3.18, which closes with מְאֻשָּֽׁר (oshb:Prov.3.18), a participle sharing the same root as the opening אַשְׁרֵ֣י and forming a root-level inclusio around the personal-benefit half of the poem (more precious than jewels, length of days, riches, pleasant paths, a tree of life). The petuchah after Prov.3.18 (oshb:Prov.3.18, single-witness) falls at that inclusio's close. The couplet at 3.19-3.20 extends the poem from personal benefit to cosmic scope -- יְֽהוָ֗ה (oshb:Prov.3.19) founding the earth and establishing the heavens by wisdom and understanding -- before the row ends at the return to second-person address at 3.21.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Ending the row at 3.18, with the petuchah there (oshb:Prov.3.18, single-witness) as the boundary, was considered and set aside: 3.19-3.20 continue third-person wisdom-praise rather than opening a new address, so the mark reads as an internal inclusio-close rather than the poem's outer edge.

next_row.boundary_rationale: Five consecutive prohibition imperatives open at 3.27 and run through 3.31, each addressing conduct toward another party -- withholding good from its owner (3.27), delaying a neighbor's due (3.28), plotting against a neighbor (3.29), needless strife (3.30), and envy of a violent man (3.31) -- a list-register run distinguishing this unit from the self-directed wisdom-keeping of 3.21-3.26. Three of the five verses carry ketiv/qere notes (3.27, 3.28, 3.30) and 3.28 also carries a paseq, all single-witness disclosure objects internal to the row; none functions as a boundary driver. The row ends before 3.32, where a two-letter conjunction introduces a shift from second-person prohibition to third-person gnomic rationale.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the five-verse prohibition list into narrower pairs (for example 3.27-3.28 / 3.29-3.31) was considered and set aside: no parashah or disclosure object marks an interior boundary, and all five verses share one prohibition-imperative construction. Reading 3.27 as a tov-min ('better than') comparative is a mandated rival to disclose: 3.27 is itself a ketiv/qere verse (oshb:Prov.3.27, disclosed above), and its contiguous טוב מ skeleton pairs with a source-marked object ('withhold good from its owner') rather than the comparative construction shared by the sweep's three other hits, Prov.15.16, Prov.16.8, and Prov.16.16.

queue_items.claim: '3 of 4 lecture-openers in this part (3.1, 3.21, 4.10, 4.20)' is arithmetically false against its own list: all four carry the singular vocative.
queue_items.grounds: Every verse the row lists is a bni_address ref in prov_device_inventory.json and the singular vocative is byte-present in each: word 1 of oshb:Prov.3.1 is בְּ֭נִי, word 1 of oshb:Prov.3.21 is בְּ֭נִי, words 1-2 of oshb:Prov.4.10 are שְׁמַ֣ע בְּ֭נִי and word 1 of oshb:Prov.4.20 is בְּ֭נִי - all at byte tier, so the ratio is 4 of 4. Read the other way, as four openers out of a set that also contains this row's own plural opener at Prov.4.1, it would be 4 of 5; on neither reading is the shipped digit right, and the row never names the count object that would decide it (verse-initial opener vs the inventory's any-position vocative verse, of which Prov.3.1-Prov.4.27 holds five, Prov.3.11 included). The seam does not depend on the digit: the contrast the row actually needs is the plural שִׁמְע֣וּ בָ֭נִים (oshb:Prov.4.1, words 1-2, byte tier) against those singular openers, and that is byte-true whatever the tally.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair in text register with the object named: e.g. 'a plural address, against the singular vocative opening Prov.3.1, Prov.3.21, Prov.4.10 and Prov.4.20 (4 of 4 verse-initial openers across Prov.3-4)'; remove 'in this part' from boundary_rationale and the row-set reference from device_notes.

trigger_dispositions.grounds: Honest and byte-anchored. The back seam is genuinely the weak one and the row says exactly why: the quoted paternal instruction opens inside Prov.4.4 with וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לִ֗י (oshb:Prov.4.4, words 2-3, byte tier) and runs on past the row's edge, so the seam rests on a speech-frame device with no corroboration available - pmarks_Prov.json carries no mark, no paseq and no K/Q anywhere in Prov.4.1-Prov.4.4 (nearest are the PE at Prov.3.35, correctly disclosed as the previous unit's, and the K/Q at Prov.4.16), precisely as the row states. The front seam is strong and byte-true: שִׁמְע֣וּ בָ֭נִים (oshb:Prov.4.1, words 1-2, byte tier) is a plural address against the singular vocative of the neighbouring openers. The straddling quotation is disclosed on both sides of the seam, the following row recording that its opening 'inherits the reported-speech frame established in 4.4, outside its own span', which satisfies the cross-seam cohesion rule. medium_low with frontier_flag_considered true is the right band; nothing defective is hiding under it.

TEST 1 fails twice - 'in this part' in boundary_rationale and 'in this part's rows' in device_notes both describe the writer's work unit and the row set rather than the text. TEST 2 fails on the digit: '3 of 4 lecture-openers in this part (3.1, 3.21, 4.10, 4.20)' contradicts its own enumeration, since all four listed verses carry the singular vocative. Recorded as the medium finding below.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: שִׁמְע֣וּ בָ֭נִים (oshb:Prov.4.1) ('listen, sons') opens chapter 4 with a plural address, distinct from the singular address term shared by 3 of 4 lecture-openers in this part (3.1, 3.21, 4.10, 4.20). The row sets up a father's instruction (4.1-4.2), then recounts his own childhood as an only son (4.3) before introducing his own father's reported words with וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לִ֗י (oshb:Prov.4.4) ('and he said to me') in 4.4, a speech-frame device that itself completes one admonition-plus-consequence couplet. The row ends there, before the quoted instruction's own imperative pair opens fresh at 4.5.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping 4.1-4.9 as one unit was considered: nothing marks 4.4/4.5 with a parashah or disclosure object, so the seam rests on the speech-frame device alone (וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לִ֗י (oshb:Prov.4.4)) rather than corroborated tier-1-plus-tier-3 evidence, which is why this boundary is held at lower confidence rather than folded together.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A two-letter conjunction (oshb:Prov.3.32) opens 3.32 and shifts the discourse from the second-person prohibition series of 3.27-3.31 to four third-person gnomic statements pairing the divine name's disposition (יְהוָ֣ה, oshb:Prov.3.32; יְ֭הוָה, oshb:Prov.3.33) with a human outcome: abomination versus friendship (3.32), curse versus blessing (3.33), mockery versus grace (3.34), and glory versus shame (3.35). The row closes at the petuchah after Prov.3.35 (oshb:Prov.3.35, single-witness), the last verse before chapter 4 opens with a plural address at 4.1.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 3.32-3.35 into the same unit as 3.27-3.31 was set aside: the conjunction opening 3.32 (oshb:Prov.3.32) marks a discourse turn to rationale-giving, and the shift from second-person imperative to third-person gnomic statement is a construction change the shared 'conduct toward another' theme alone would not justify keeping together.

next_row.boundary_rationale: The quoted paternal instruction introduced at the close of 4.4 continues here with a fresh imperative pair, קְנֵ֣ה חָ֭כְמָה קְנֵ֣ה בִינָ֑ה (oshb:Prov.4.5) ('get wisdom, get understanding'), echoed again within 4.7 (oshb:Prov.4.7) -- split as קְנֵ֣ה חָכְמָ֑ה (4.7's 3rd-4th words) and קְנֵ֣ה בִינָֽה (4.7's final two words), divided by וּבְכָל קִ֝נְיָנְךָ֗ -- an internal repetition bracketing 4.5-4.7 before the row closes with wisdom personified as a figure who exalts, honors, and crowns the one who embraces her (4.8-4.9). No disclosure object falls inside this span. The row ends before the part's third lecture-opener at 4.10.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting 4.5-4.7 from the personification lines of 4.8-4.9 was considered and set aside: the repeated קְנֵ֣ה חָ֭כְמָה קְנֵ֣ה בִינָ֑ה (oshb:Prov.4.5) imperative and the result clauses that follow it read as one continuous appeal rather than two, so no interior seam is argued here.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: Both verses turn on the same word for its end/latter part -- וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ (oshb:Prov.14.12) and וְאַחֲרִיתָ֖הּ (oshb:Prov.14.13), byte tier -- functioning both times as the pivot from an opening observation to its outcome: a way that seems right before a man, but its end is the ways of death (14:12); even in laughter a heart may ache, and the end of joy is grief (14:13). A second, independently named ground supports the pairing alongside the hinge-word: both verses share the identical appearance-vs-outcome template (what seems/is X in the moment ends in Y), naming the shared structure rather than resting the pairing on the hinge-word alone.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping these as two separate rows was considered, since both verses are grammatically complete on their own; the pair was adopted instead because the shared hinge-word is the operative word of both verses' arguments, not a passing vocabulary overlap, giving it more weight than the one-token catchword pairs at Prov.12.18-Prov.12.19 and Prov.13.19-Prov.13.20. The identical proverb recurs verbatim at Prov.16.25 (byte tier); that duplicate is disclosed as counter-evidence for any claim of a construction unique to this seam, though it does not by itself unseat the pairing argued here.

queue_items.claim: The disclaimer that the verse 'shares no lexeme' with Prov.13.1-13.2 is byte-false: it shares two lexemes with Prov.13.2.
queue_items.grounds: boundary_rationale asserts the verse 'is not adjacent to those and shares no lexeme with them'. Skeleton content-token comparison from consonantal_index.json: Prov.14.14 and Prov.13.2 share TWO tokens. oshb:Prov.13.2 carries אִ֭ישׁ and ט֑וֹב; oshb:Prov.14.14 carries אִ֣ישׁ and טֽוֹב - the same two lexemes, differing only in accents. Prov.13.1 does share nothing with Prov.14.14, so the claim is false for one of the two verses it names, not both. It is a no-class universal shipped without a digit, and check_universals does not carry this phrasing in its lexicon, so it passed Tier-0 unflagged. It is not load-bearing - the boundary rests on the in-verse ellipsis and the rejected alternative rests on the compound noun's gloss being unnecessary - hence medium, not high.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair to boundary_rationale: strike the disclaimer, or correct it to name the two shared lexemes and state that the shared vocabulary is generic and non-adjacent, so the comparison is not a cohesion claim.

Strategy S7 places lexical cruxes in the expected-low-confidence class and requires bespoke uncertainty text; this row's text is row-specific rather than boilerplate, and frontier_flag_considered is true. The band is neither over-stated nor masking a byte-defective warrant, so the trigger itself is not a defect; the byte-false comparison claim in this row is recorded separately as a finding.
